title: Operation Quiet Harbor

victim.name: Daniel Okafor
victim.occupation: Harbor customs broker, Okafor & Vance Brokerage
victim.description: A tall, careful man known for keeping meticulous ledgers and for never missing his daughter's Saturday swim meets. Found dead in his office at the brokerage.
victim.background: Okafor had spent nineteen years clearing cargo through the Port Ellery container terminal. In the last year he had grown quieter, cancelled a family holiday, and started staying late. He had recently met twice with a Customs and Border Protection liaison, which is why the Bureau has the case: the killing appears connected to a federal smuggling investigation he was quietly assisting.

crime.summary: Daniel Okafor was found dead at his desk at Okafor & Vance Brokerage at 06:40 on Saturday 14 March by the cleaner. A single gunshot wound to the chest. The office safe was open and empty.
crime.whatReallyHappened: Okafor's business partner Marcus Vance had been clearing containers for a smuggling ring and skimming fees, using Okafor's signature stamps. Okafor discovered the discrepancy in late February, confronted Vance on 12 March, and told him he was taking the ledgers to CBP on Monday the 16th. On Friday night 13 March, Vance returned to the office at 23:10 using his own key, after telling his wife he was at a bar in Cutter Street. He argued with Okafor, who was working late, and shot him once with a .38 revolver he had bought unregistered in 2024. He emptied the safe to stage a robbery, took the original ledgers, and left by the rear loading door, which he wedged shut badly. He dumped the ledgers in a marina dumpster behind Pier 9, but kept the revolver in a tackle box on his boat, the Second Wind. His car was caught on a toll gantry on the Harbor Spur at 23:02 and again at 23:51, which contradicts his claim to have been at the Anchor Bar until 00:30.

timeline.event: Okafor finds fee discrepancies in container clearances carrying his stamp.
Okafor meets CBP liaison Ruth Alder for the second time.
Okafor confronts Vance in the office; a raised-voice argument is overheard by receptionist Lena Bright.
Okafor tells his wife he will work late to finish copying documents.
Tomas Reyes, a dockworker Okafor fired, is seen shouting outside the brokerage, then leaves for the Anchor Bar.
Vance's car passes the Harbor Spur toll gantry inbound.
Vance shoots Okafor, empties the safe, takes the ledgers, leaves by the rear door.
Vance's car passes the toll gantry outbound.
Cleaner Ana Petrov finds the body and calls 911.

suspects.name: Marcus Vance
suspects.background: Co-founded the brokerage with Okafor in 2009. Charming, a known gambler at the Riverside casino, two mortgages. Sits on the harbor business council.
suspects.personality: Smooth, expansive, performs grief, always redirects to how much he loved Danny.
suspects.speechStyle: Polished, salesman's cadence, calls people 'friend', long answers that circle away from specifics, uses 'honestly' a lot.
suspects.secret: Deep gambling debts to a private lender.

alibi.claim: At the Anchor Bar on Cutter Street from about 22:00 until 00:30, then home.
alibi.whatActuallyHappened: Left the bar at 22:45, drove to the brokerage, killed Okafor, drove home via the Harbor Spur.

suspects.motiveIfAny: Okafor was about to expose his fraud to CBP.
suspects.criminalHistory: No record. Two civil judgments for unpaid debts (2023, 2025).
suspects.vehicle: 2022 dark grey Audi Q5, MD plate 7KX-4420
suspects.phoneRecordsSummary: Phone was powered off from 22:40 to 00:05 on 13 March. Four calls to an unlisted number (a private lender) in the preceding week.
suspects.financialsSummary: $180,000 in casino markers; three cash deposits of $9,500 each in February from an unknown source; brokerage account shows fee skimming routed through a shell, Tidewater Clearing LLC.

suspects.name: Tomas Reyes
suspects.background: Fired by Okafor two weeks before the killing after a container seal was found broken on his shift. Hot-tempered, two kids, lives with his mother in Cutter Street.
suspects.personality: Angry, wounded pride, quick to feel accused, but honest.
suspects.speechStyle: Short, blunt sentences, swears when cornered, Spanish phrases when upset.
suspects.relationshipToVictim: Former employee; blamed Okafor for the firing.
suspects.secret: He broke the seal himself because a man paid him $500 to look away; he is ashamed and afraid.

alibi.claim: At the Anchor Bar from about 21:50 until closing at 01:00.
alibi.whatActuallyHappened: Was at the Anchor Bar the whole time, drunk, as the bartender and bar CCTV confirm.

suspects.phoneRecordsSummary: Phone pinged the Cutter Street tower all night. Several angry texts to a friend about Okafor at 21:30.
suspects.financialsSummary: Overdrawn. One $500 cash deposit on 1 March.

suspects.name: Grace Okafor
suspects.background: Married to the victim for twenty years. Composed, exhausted, protective of her daughter. Recently took out a large life insurance policy on both spouses.
suspects.speechStyle: Quiet, clinical vocabulary, pauses before answering, corrects imprecision.
suspects.secret: She had consulted a divorce lawyer in January, before Daniel's withdrawal made sense to her.

alibi.claim: At home with their daughter Imani all evening; asleep by 23:00.
alibi.whatActuallyHappened: At home. Daughter and a neighbour's doorbell camera confirm the car never left.

suspects.motiveIfAny: A $1.2 million life insurance policy taken out in January.
suspects.phoneRecordsSummary: Phone at home all night. Calls to a divorce attorney in January.
suspects.financialsSummary: Life insurance policy on both spouses purchased 20 January; premiums paid; nothing else unusual.

suspects.name: Ruth Alder
suspects.background: The federal officer Okafor had been quietly talking to. Ambitious, under internal review for a leak in a prior case.
suspects.personality: Guarded, bureaucratic, resents the Bureau taking over.
suspects.speechStyle: Formal, acronym-heavy, answers only the question asked.
suspects.secret: She told her supervisor about Okafor only after his death; she had been sitting on his information hoping to build the case herself.

alibi.claim: At the CBP port office until 22:30, then home in Glenmoor.
alibi.whatActuallyHappened: Badge logs and the port office camera confirm it.

suspects.motiveIfAny: If Okafor's information embarrassed her, her career was over.
suspects.vehicle: 2020 black Jeep Cherokee, government plate G-44-1187
suspects.phoneRecordsSummary: Two calls from Okafor on 13 March at 19:10 and 20:55, both unanswered.

suspects.name: Eli Branagh
suspects.background: Works nights at the marina next to the brokerage. Small-time weed dealer, nervous around police.
suspects.personality: Jittery, eager to please, forgets things when scared.
suspects.relationshipToVictim: Knew him by sight; Okafor sometimes parked at the marina.
suspects.secret: Deals cannabis to boat owners, including Vance.

alibi.claim: In the marina office all night, watching movies.
alibi.whatActuallyHappened: In the office; the marina camera shows him. He saw Vance's Audi at 23:05 and a man carrying something to the dumpster at 23:40 but did not look closely.

suspects.phoneRecordsSummary: Texts with several boat owners about 'the usual'. One text to Vance on 11 March: 'got your usual, come by'.

culprit.motive: Okafor had discovered that Vance was skimming fees and clearing containers for a smuggling ring using Okafor's stamps, and intended to hand the ledgers to CBP on Monday.
culprit.means: An unregistered .38 revolver Vance had owned since 2024, kept on his boat.
culprit.opportunity: He had his own key to the office; he left the Anchor Bar at 22:45, not 00:30, and his car hit the Harbor Spur toll gantry inbound at 23:02 and outbound at 23:51.
culprit.howItWasDone: Vance let himself in, argued, shot Okafor once at close range, emptied the safe to stage a robbery, took the original ledgers, left through the rear loading door, dumped the ledgers in the Pier 9 dumpster and hid the revolver in a tackle box aboard his boat.

evidence.name: Spent .38 bullet
evidence.exactSpot: recovered by ERT from the wall panel behind the desk
evidence.description: A deformed lead bullet in an evidence bag, tagged by ERT.
closeLookReveals: Deformed but with clear rifling; six lands and grooves, right twist.
No jacket; an old-style lead round, the kind sold for revolvers.

lab.ballistics: Consistent with a .38 Special fired from a revolver with six right-twist lands and grooves. Suitable for comparison if a weapon is recovered.

evidence.significance: Will match the revolver on Vance's boat.

evidence.name: Open office safe
evidence.exactSpot: the safe behind the desk, door open
evidence.description: A floor safe, door standing open, empty inside.
closeLookReveals: No tool marks, no scratches: it was opened with the combination, not forced.
A faint rectangular dust outline inside: something book-sized was removed.

lab.fingerprints: Latent prints on the dial belong to the victim and to Marcus Vance. Vance's presence is unremarkable on its own; he is a partner.

evidence.significance: Opened by someone who knew the combination: Okafor or Vance.

evidence.name: Rear loading door wedge
evidence.exactSpot: the rear loading door at the back of the warehouse bay, a folded cardboard wedge in the frame
evidence.description: A folded piece of cardboard jammed in the rear door frame so the door would not latch.
closeLookReveals: The cardboard is from a Riverside Casino drinks carton.
A partial muddy shoe print on the step outside, a dress-shoe sole, size 11 or 12.

lab.trace: Mud on the step contains marina silt consistent with Pier 9.

evidence.significance: The killer left by the rear door and went toward the marina.

evidence.name: Okafor's desk calendar
evidence.exactSpot: under the blotter on the desk
evidence.description: A paper desk calendar with cramped handwriting.
closeLookReveals: Monday 16 March: 'R.A. 9am - bring originals'.
Thursday 12 March: 'M. - talk. Enough.' underlined twice.
evidence.significance: He planned to hand the ledgers to Ruth Alder on Monday and had confronted 'M.' on Thursday.

evidence.name: Anchor Bar CCTV export
evidence.exactSpot: the bar's DVR behind the counter; the bartender will export it on request
evidence.description: A USB stick with the bar's camera footage for the night of 13 March.
closeLookReveals: Tomas Reyes is visible at the bar from 21:52 until he is helped out at 00:58.
Marcus Vance is visible arriving at 22:03 and leaving through the side door at 22:44.

lab.digital: Timestamps verified against the DVR clock, which is accurate to within one minute.

evidence.significance: Breaks Vance's alibi and confirms Reyes's.

evidence.name: Harbor Spur toll gantry records
evidence.exactSpot: the toll authority office; records released on subpoena or formal request
evidence.description: A printout of plate reads from the Harbor Spur gantry on 13 March.
closeLookReveals: MD 7KX-4420 (Vance's Audi) inbound 23:02, outbound 23:51.
No read for MD 2RT-9981 (Reyes's truck) or MD 5GH-2210 (Grace Okafor's Subaru).
evidence.significance: Places Vance's car at the harbor during the killing.

evidence.name: Water-damaged ledgers
evidence.exactSpot: inside the marina dumpster behind Pier 9, under fish-house waste
evidence.description: Two bound ledgers, soaked and stinking, Okafor & Vance letterhead.
closeLookReveals: Entries show clearance fees paid to 'Tidewater Clearing LLC' against containers stamped with Okafor's number.
Marginal notes in Okafor's hand: 'not mine', 'MV?'

lab.documents: Ink analysis shows the marginal notes were made within the last six weeks. Signature stamps on the flagged entries were applied with Okafor's stamp but the initialling is in Vance's hand.
lab.fingerprints: Vance's prints on the covers over the victim's.

evidence.significance: The motive: the fraud Okafor had uncovered.

evidence.name: .38 revolver in tackle box
evidence.exactSpot: a tackle box in the stern locker of the boat Second Wind
evidence.description: A blued .38 Special revolver wrapped in a rag inside a tackle box.
closeLookReveals: Five live rounds and one spent casing still in the cylinder.
Serial number partly filed.

lab.ballistics: Test-fired bullets match the bullet recovered from the scene (e1): same lands, grooves and individual striations.
lab.fingerprints: Partial print on the cylinder release consistent with Marcus Vance.

evidence.name: Life insurance policy
evidence.exactSpot: a folder in the filing cabinet in the home office
evidence.description: A $1.2 million joint life insurance policy dated 20 January 2026.
closeLookReveals: Both spouses are insured; both signed.
The agent's note says it was bought alongside a will revision after Daniel's father died.
evidence.significance: Red herring: ordinary estate planning after a death in the family.

evidence.name: Reyes's angry texts
evidence.exactSpot: on Reyes's phone, which he will show if asked without pressure
closeLookReveals: 'gonna tell okafor what i think of him tonight'.
'screw it im drinking' at 21:49.
evidence.significance: Red herring: he shouted outside and then went to drink.

locations.name: Okafor & Vance Brokerage
locations.description: A two-storey brick building between the container terminal and the marina. The ground floor is a warehouse bay; the office upstairs smells of coffee, toner and, now, the chemical tang of ERT. Okafor's desk faces the door. The safe behind it gapes open.
sharpEyeDetails: The front door was locked when the cleaner arrived; whoever left did not go out the front.
A rectangular clean patch on the desk where something book-sized sat.
locations.canvassYields: The marina night manager saw a dark SUV around 23:00; a fish-house worker heard a 'bang like a pallet dropping' around 23:15.

locations.name: Okafor residence
locations.description: A tidy colonial with a swim-team banner in the window. Grace keeps the house running with a stillness that feels like effort. Daniel's home office is untouched.
sharpEyeDetails: A neighbour's doorbell camera faces the driveway.
A stack of photocopies on the home office printer: pages of a ledger.
locations.canvassYields: The neighbour's doorbell camera shows Grace's car never left between 19:00 and 07:00.

locations.name: Anchor Bar
locations.description: A dockworkers' bar with a sticky floor and a camera over the till that the owner is proud of. The bartender, Sal, remembers everyone.
sharpEyeDetails: Camera covers the bar and the side door.
A side door leads to the alley where regulars park.
locations.canvassYields: Sal says Reyes was there all night and 'the brokerage guy, the smooth one' left early 'like he had somewhere to be'.

locations.name: Pier 9 Marina
locations.description: Floating docks, halyards ticking against masts, a dumpster behind the fish house that nobody empties on time. The night office has a camera on the gate.
sharpEyeDetails: Tyre marks in the silt by the dumpster.
The gate camera points at the lot.
searchableAreas: the dumpster behind the fish house
locations.canvassYields: Eli Branagh, the night manager, saw a dark Audi at 23:05 and someone carrying something heavy to the dumpster around 23:40.

locations.name: Harbor Spur toll authority
locations.description: A grey office that smells of carpet glue. Plate-read records are released only with legal process.
sharpEyeDetails: The gantry reads every plate between the city and the harbor.

locations.name: Boat 'Second Wind', slip 22
locations.description: A 32-foot cruiser, well kept, Vance's name on the registration. Fishing gear in the stern locker.
sharpEyeDetails: The stern locker padlock is new.
A Riverside Casino drinks carton in the cockpit trash.
locations.canvassYields: Neighbouring boat owner says Vance came by late Friday, 'after midnight, which he never does'.

witnesses.name: Lena Bright
witnesses.speechStyle: Chatty, loyal to both partners, hedges.
witnesses.whatTheySaw: Heard Okafor and Vance shouting in the office on Thursday 12 March; caught the words 'CBP' and 'you'll ruin us'.
witnesses.bias: Likes Vance, does not want to get him in trouble.
witnesses.initialStatement: Everyone loved Daniel. Things had been tense lately with the business, I think money was tight, but nothing specific. I left at 17:00 on Friday as usual.

witnesses.name: Ruth Alder (as witness)
witnesses.whatTheySaw: Okafor told her on 10 March that he had found fee discrepancies involving a shell company and would bring originals on Monday the 16th.
witnesses.bias: Protecting her own handling of the source.
witnesses.initialStatement: Mr Okafor had approached CBP with concerns about clearance irregularities at the terminal. We had scheduled a follow-up. I am not able to say more without authorisation.

witnesses.name: Ana Petrov
witnesses.whatTheySaw: Front door locked at 06:40; the rear door was not latched, which she noticed because it was cold in the bay. Saw the fired dockworker shouting outside on Friday evening around 21:40 as she left her other job nearby.
witnesses.bias: Frightened; may exaggerate the dockworker's anger.
witnesses.initialStatement: The front door was locked, I used my key. Upstairs Mr Okafor was at his desk, I thought he was asleep. The angry man from the docks was shouting outside on Friday evening, I saw him when I passed, he said bad things about Mr Okafor.

redHerrings.description: Tomas Reyes shouting outside the brokerage hours before the killing, his record, and his angry texts.
redHerrings.whyMisleading: He went to the Anchor Bar and stayed until closing; CCTV and the bartender confirm it.

redHerrings.description: The $1.2 million life insurance policy Grace Okafor took out in January.
redHerrings.whyMisleading: Ordinary estate planning after her father-in-law died; the doorbell camera shows she never left home.

redHerrings.description: Ruth Alder's defensiveness and the two unanswered calls from Okafor that evening.
redHerrings.whyMisleading: She was covering for mishandling a source, not a killing; badge logs place her at the port office.

provingClues.whatItProves: Vance left the bar at 22:44, not 00:30: his alibi is false.
His car was at the harbor at 23:02 and left at 23:51, bracketing the killing.
The revolver on his boat fired the fatal bullet and carries his print.
The ledgers he dumped establish the fraud and therefore the motive.

charges: 18 U.S.C. § 1111 murder (federal nexus: killing of a federal informant)
18 U.S.C. § 545 smuggling goods into the United States
initialReport: At 06:40 on Saturday 14 March 2026, cleaner Ana Petrov found Daniel Okafor, 47, dead at his desk on the upper floor of Okafor & Vance Brokerage, 14 Quay Street, Port Ellery. Port Ellery PD responded; the medical examiner reports a single gunshot wound to the chest, time of death between 22:00 and 01:00. The office floor safe was open and empty. The front door was locked; the rear loading door was unlatched. ERT recovered one deformed bullet from the wall panel. Okafor was a customs broker who had recently made contact with CBP regarding clearance irregularities at the container terminal, which is why the case was referred to the Baltimore Field Office. Persons known to have had contact with or grievance against the victim in the preceding week include his business partner Marcus Vance, a recently dismissed dockworker Tomas Reyes, and the CBP liaison Ruth Alder. The victim's wife, Grace Okafor, reports he told her he would be working late. No weapon recovered.
supervisorBriefing: Sit down. Daniel Okafor was talking to Customs about something dirty at the terminal and now he's dead at his desk with his safe hanging open. That is why it's ours and not Port Ellery PD's. The ME says one round to the chest, sometime after ten. No weapon. Somebody wants this to look like a robbery; I don't buy it and neither should you. You've got the partner, a dockworker Okafor fired who was screaming outside the building that night, the wife, and a CBP liaison who is already lawyering her answers. Start at the scene, then the bar on Cutter Street, and pin down where everybody actually was. Get the lab moving early; ballistics takes hours and DNA takes a day. Warrants go through me and then the magistrate, and I will not sign off on a hunch. You have seventy-two hours before the AUSA wants a theory. Go.
